Triage (R+89, triage seat, session `session_019kDRpB7D2XzVzkaLp57T5D`): **`pm:queue`** · `priority:p2` · `domain:spec` · type **Bug**.

⚠️ **Read this card through the raw/rendered page, not the MCP `issue_read` channel.** The stored body is complete (3,057 bytes, verified via the zero-quota page payload); the MCP read path drops the angle-bracket key spellings in the title and cuts the body at "Handler dispatch is an exact-string `Map` lookup on `" — a read-side artifact, ⛔ not a truncated card, so repair-first does not apply. Implementers: fetch the page or REST raw body.

**Lands in:** `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` — `defineStack`'s cross-reference walk (the seam that already refuses a `runAction` naming a non-existent action). **Ruled route:** refuse a duplicate scope-qualified action key (`objectName ?? 'global'` + name) within one stack's action set, naming the offending pair. ⛔ The cross-scope pair (one global + one object-bound of the same name) is **not** refused by this card — it occupies two keys today, and the precedence the code already implements (`resolveRouteActionDeclaration` prefers the object's embedded array) is to be written into the schema doc rather than changed; if a by-name consumer proves ambiguous in practice, that is a follow-up card with a measured consumer. Rationale: same-scope duplicates collapse to one handler key and the loser is a live, permission-gated button that fails only when clicked — the ADR-0078 shape at collection level, and exactly the copy-and-forget-to-rename edit an AI author produces.

**Clause-②: yes** — `defineStack`'s accept set narrows (a stack that parses today is refused), so the spec seat dispatches at the contract-review tier; the deliverable includes a corpus pass over the shipped example apps to show zero same-scope duplicates exist there today.

Size/model suggestion: S, `claude-fable-5` per clause ②.
